summary: Created MovieEditorView.axaml with three-column Grid layout (280px left sidebar, * center, 200px right sidebar).

Left sidebar: scrollable editable fields (Label, ActorNames, Studio, Description, Rating, Year, Season, Episode, ViewCount); fixed bottom panel with action toolbar (Apply, Save & Exit, Discard, Close, Clean Label, Properties), review section (NeedsReview status, collapsible message panel, Flag/Mark Reviewed/Reset Views buttons), and M10 Bookmarks stub.
Center: TabControl with Cover Image (M8), Thumbnails (M9), and Video (M10) tab stubs.
Right sidebar: Tagging (M7) stub.
Created MovieEditorView.axaml.cs with parameterless constructor.
Created Converters/IntDecimalConverter.cs to handle int/int? ↔ decimal? for NumericUpDown compiled bindings.
Registered MovieEditorView in Program.cs DI container via factory lambda.
Build: no errors, no warnings. Tests: 569 passed, 6 skipped (expected).

comments.note: IntDecimalConverter.cs was added to support int/int? <-> decimal? conversion for NumericUpDown compiled bindings. The project had no existing converter infrastructure; this is the first file in the new Converters/ folder. Future numeric inputs in other views can reuse this converter.

MovieEditorView.axaml: MoveActorUp/Down buttons (▲▼) are rendered but will always be no-ops because SelectedActorName is never populated — the view binds ActorNamesText as a plain TextBox with no ListBox for actor selection. The ViewModel already handles null gracefully, but the buttons are misleading. A future WP could either wire a ListBox (with a split-string converter) or remove the buttons from the toolbar.

The left sidebar's fixed bottom panel (action toolbar + review section) is not scrollable. If the review collapsible panel is open and the window is short, the lower controls (Confirm/Cancel) could be clipped. A future layout refinement could wrap the entire sidebar in a single ScrollViewer or use a minimum window height constraint.

summary: Code review PASS with one Fix-Forward applied. All five acceptance criteria confirmed met. Implementation is clean, well-structured, and follows established project conventions.

Fix-Forward applied: added IsEnabled='False' to the MoveActorUp/Down buttons in MovieEditorView.axaml. The buttons were always no-ops (SelectedActorName is never set by the view — no ListBox exists), yet appeared enabled, misleading users. This is a non-behavioral UX clarity fix; QA validation remains intact. Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

IntDecimalConverter: singleton pattern (Instance) is correct and well-documented. The AXAML creates its own resource instance (standard Avalonia pattern); Instance is available for code-based use. ConvertBack handles int/int? target types cleanly. No issues.

MovieEditorViewModel: Backing-field initialization in the full constructor avoids spurious PropertyChanged notifications — good practice. BuildMovieFromCurrentState() uses record with {} correctly per constraints.md. The nullable _movieRepository design for the parameterless constructor is a clean no-op guard pattern.

Program.cs: AddTransient<MovieEditorView>(_ => new MovieEditorView()) is correct, consistent with other view registrations, and the _ => factory discards the SP appropriately since MovieEditorView has no DI dependencies.
Reviewed files: MovieEditorView.axaml, MovieEditorView.axaml.cs, IntDecimalConverter.cs, Program.cs (MovieEditorView registration), MovieEditorViewModel.cs (context).

comments.note: MovieEditorView.axaml: Added IsEnabled='False' to the MoveActorUp (▲) and MoveActorDown (▼) buttons. These buttons have no selection mechanism wired in the view (SelectedActorName is never populated — no ListBox exists), so they were always no-ops while appearing fully enabled. Disabling them visually communicates their stub status and prevents user confusion. Non-behavioral change; ViewModel null guards remain intact. Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

IntDecimalConverter: Instance singleton and AXAML resource instance coexist correctly. The static Instance property enables future code-based use without allocations; the AXAML resource instance follows the standard converter resource pattern. When actor-list management is fully implemented (ListBox + split-string converter), consider whether a dedicated ActorListConverter should also live in Converters/.

[documentation-forward] IntDecimalConverter.cs is the first file in the new src/VideoIndexer.App/Converters/ folder. The api-surface.md manifest should document the converter class signature (Convert/ConvertBack), its role as the int↔decimal? bridge for NumericUpDown compiled bindings, and the singleton Instance usage pattern. The file-tree.md should also reflect the new Converters/ directory.

MovieEditorViewModel: CancelSetReview does not clear ReviewMessage, so a partially-typed but cancelled message persists in the backing field. Next time the Flag panel opens, the stale draft will be pre-populated in the TextBox. Consider clearing ReviewMessage to null (or restoring the original value) in CancelSetReview — out of scope for this stub WP but worth tracking for M6 polish.
